### Generating the lexer and parser

# While there is some autoconf macro support for lex/flex, it doesn't support
# header file creation so we'll use good old make
if MAINTAINER_MODE
BUILT_SOURCES = src/lexer.h src/lexer.c src/parser.h src/parser.c 	\
		src/builtin.inc src/version.h
src/lexer.c: src/lexer.l
	$(AM_V_LEX) flex -o src/lexer.c --header-file=src/lexer.h $<
src/lexer.h: src/lexer.c
else
BUILT_SOURCES = src/builtin.inc src/version.h
.y.c:
	$(AM_V_YACC) echo "NOT building parser.c!"
.l.c:

part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in the grammar in `src/parser.y`: `ElseBody` required a trailing `"else" Exp "end"`, and the optional-else case was only handled by a separate `"if" Exp "then" Exp "end"` rule that couldn't be combined with `elif`.

Changes:
- `src/parser.y:367` — the `if` rule now consumes the final `"end"` itself: `"if" Exp "then" Exp ElseBody "end"`.
- `src/parser.y:622` — `ElseBody` now allows `%empty` (maps to `gen_noop()`, i.e. identity for the false branch), `"elif" Exp "then" Exp ElseBody`, or `"else" Exp`.
- `src/parser.c` and `src/parser.h` regenerated with bison 3.8.2 (no conflicts).

Verified: `1,2,3 | if . == 1 then 1 elif . == 2 then 2 end` now outputs `1 2 3`, works with `else`, plain `if...end`, unterminated-`if` error messages are preserved, and `make check` passes all 21 tests (jqtest, shtest, mantest, onigtest, utf8test, base64test, etc.).
